question: What is the primary purpose of a unidirectional workflow in the operating room environment?

options.A: To speed up the movement of surgical instruments
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination between clean and contaminated areas
options.C: To ensure patients spend less time in the surgical suite
options.D: To reduce the electricity consumption of the surgical lights

explanation: A unidirectional workflow organizes the movement of staff, patients, and supplies to prevent cross-contamination and maintain safety. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why are operating room walls, floors, and ceilings designed with non-porous surfaces?

options.A: To withstand frequent and rigorous disinfection
options.B: To improve the acoustic quality for music playing
options.C: To reflect maximum light into the surgical wound
options.D: To lower the cost of initial facility construction

explanation: Non-porous surfaces are used because they do not absorb moisture and can withstand rigorous cleaning and disinfection. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which operating theatre zone permits the wearing of ordinary street clothes?
explanation: The unrestricted area acts as a transition zone where street clothes are permitted before entering the scrub and changing areas. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h2)

question: What attire is mandatory when entering the semi-restricted area of the surgical suite?

options.A: Complete sterile surgical gown and gloves
options.B: Surgical scrubs, dedicated footwear, and hair covers
options.C: Ordinary street clothes with a lab coat
options.D: Heavy lead aprons and sterile shoe covers

explanation: Personnel in the semi-restricted area must wear surgical scrubs, dedicated footwear, and hair covers to minimize contaminants. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h2)

question: What type of air pressure is maintained inside the operating room relative to the surrounding corridors?
explanation: Positive pressure ensures air flows outward from the OR into corridors, preventing contaminated air from entering the sterile space. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary function of HEPA filters in the operating room HVAC system?

options.A: To humidify the dry air entering the surgical suite
options.B: To remove microscopic particles, dust, and airborne microorganisms
options.C: To cool down the surgical lights during long procedures
options.D: To increase the concentration of oxygen in the room

explanation: HEPA filters are designed to capture microscopic particles, dust, and airborne microorganisms to maintain high air purity. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why must an operating table often be radiolucent during certain procedures?

options.A: To prevent electrical shocks from the electrosurgical unit
options.B: To allow intraoperative imaging such as X-rays to pass through
options.C: To keep the patient warm during long surgeries
options.D: to repel airborne dust particles from settling

explanation: Radiolucent operating tables allow imaging equipment like X-ray machines to capture images without obstruction from the table material. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h4)

question: What is a crucial safety precaution when using an electrosurgical unit (diathermy) in the OR?

options.A: Ensuring the correct placement of the patient grounding pad
options.B: Turning off all overhead surgical lights
options.C: Connecting the unit to a portable oxygen cylinder
options.D: Using ungrounded power outlets for the device

explanation: Correct placement of the patient grounding pad prevents electrical current from causing patient burns during electrosurgery. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h4)

question: What action should be taken if there is any doubt about the sterility of an item in the operating room?

options.A: Wipe it down with alcohol and use it immediately
options.B: Assume it is contaminated and discard or re-sterilize it
options.C: Ask the surgeon if it looks safe to use
options.D: Place it on the edge of the sterile field

explanation: If there is any doubt regarding the sterility of an item, it must be considered contaminated and discarded to protect the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h5)

question: How should sterile team members pass each other within the sterile area to maintain sterility?
explanation: Sterile personnel should always pass back-to-back or face-to-face to avoid accidental contamination of sterile gowns. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h5)

question: What three elements make up the surgical fire triad present in many operating rooms?

options.C: Anesthetic gas, sterile drape, and patient blood

explanation: A surgical fire requires an ignition source, an oxidizer (like oxygen), and fuel (like drapes) to occur simultaneously. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which medication is critical for the immediate emergency treatment of malignant hyperthermia in the OR?
explanation: Dantrolene is the specific muscle relaxant and antidote used to treat life-threatening malignant hyperthermia crises. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary role of the scrub nurse within the operating room?

options.A: Managing the non-sterile environment and documentation
options.B: Operating within the sterile field to handle instruments and assist the surgeon
options.C: Administering general anesthesia to the patient
options.D: Transporting the patient to and from the recovery ward

explanation: The scrub nurse works in the sterile field, handing instruments to the surgeon and keeping track of counts. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h7)

question: Which team member functions in a non-sterile role outside the sterile boundary to coordinate the overall OR environment?
explanation: The circulating nurse works outside the sterile field to monitor the environment, document care, and coordinate communication. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h7)
